CogMap — self-repairing cognitive maps for robots

Phone walkthrough → world model → simulated swarm learns to navigate → the world changes → the swarm's failures repair the map → success recovers. Every map version is a W&B Weave evaluation.

Reflector post-mortem (gpt-5)

Round 1 — desk_2 blocked the chokepoint at (57, 55), degrading performance: success rate dropped to 0.875 with 24 collisions and 61 failures (v1-after-change-1, SPL 0.763875). Evidence came from high collision/failure spikes on the busiest corridor and 97 new cells learned by exploration (no patrol preemption). One repair pass applied 5 rule ops (0 LLM ops applied, 1 rejected); recovery took 737 steps, restoring success to 1.0 (v2-repaired-1.1) and updating the map to version 3. Round 2 — the desk (goal of 4 tasks) moved to (40, 68), causing success to dip to 0.75 with 9 collisions and 15 failures (v3-after-change-2, SPL 0.7333125). The swarm confirmed the relocation via task failures and 87 exploratory cell updates (no patrol preemption). One repair used 7 rule ops (no LLM ops), costing 1227 steps; success returned to 1.0 (v4-repaired-2.1), and the map advanced to version 5. Round 3 — desk_2 was removed from the corridor, but the map still showed a block. Patrol preempted the issue and corrected 5 cells before tasks, yet post-change metrics showed 7 collisions and 45 failures despite success 1.0 (v6-after-change-3, SPL 0.8714375), indicating residual routing mismatches. One repair with 7 rule ops (no LLM ops) reconciled the map in 737 steps, restoring SPL to 0.948375 with zero collisions/failures (v7-repaired-3.1) and updating to map version 8; 38 cells were learned by exploration. What the swarm learned — The chokepoint at (57, 55) is highly volatile and high-impact; object moves there rapidly degrade safety and throughput. Task-goal relocations (e.g., desk to (40, 68)) propagate widely across routes. Map staleness after obstacle removal can persist and cause avoidable collisions. Prioritize patrols on: (a) the (57, 55) corridor and its feeder lanes, (b) paths to/from (40, 68), and (c) recently cleared segments to catch reversions. Patrol preemption in Round 3 proved effective; expanding targeted chokepoint patrols should reduce recovery steps and collision spikes in future rounds.
